matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: First compute the decimal values of both sides of the equation (including any operators). Determine the numeric imbalance and use it to decide which single‑stick move can correct the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Always at the start of solving a matchstick puzzle, before attempting any stick relocation.
matchstick.example: Computing the numeric values incorrectly and moving a stick without considering the imbalance, resulting in a numerically false equation.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must increase contains a V and the numeric imbalance is exactly +5, reposition one of the V’s diagonal sticks so that it crosses the other stick, turning the V into an X (value +5).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is +5 and a V is present on the side that needs to increase.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a V but leaving the V as a single diagonal, creating an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that already has at least one I to another numeral that can accept an additional I, adjusting values by ±1 per stick moved.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is ±1 and both sides contain numerals with removable or addable I sticks.
matchstick.example: Removing an I from a numeral that only has one I, leaving an empty numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must decrease contains an X and the numeric imbalance is exactly –5, reposition one of the X’s diagonal sticks so that it no longer crosses, turning the X into a V (value –5). Ensure the resulting numeral string remains a valid Roman numeral (e.g., avoid creating duplicate V).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is –5 and an X is present on the side that needs to decrease.
matchstick.example: Converting X to V but ending up with ‘VVIII’, which violates Roman‑numeral rules.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) appear, you can move one horizontal from the equals sign to the minus sign, turning the minus into an equals and the equals into a minus while preserving a single equality sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '-' and '=', and the numeric imbalance suggests such a swap could balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' to '-' and ending up with no equality sign, breaking the equation.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Remove the vertical stick from a plus sign; the remaining horizontal becomes a minus sign, changing addition to subtraction and adjusting the numeric result accordingly.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When changing '+' to '-' would correct the numeric imbalance; ensure the equality sign remains intact.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' and forgetting to adjust the numeric balance, leaving the equation false.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When relocating a stick from the equality sign, ensure at least one horizontal stick remains so that the sign stays a valid '=', otherwise the equation loses its equality operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any move that takes a stick from the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal from '=', leaving only one horizontal, which becomes a minus sign and removes the equality.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality when imbalance is 2
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides is exactly 2, move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the larger side to a numeral on the smaller side, adjusting both sides by 1 each and preserving equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and both sides contain numerals with removable and addable I sticks.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a numeral that cannot lose it, making the source numeral empty.

matchstick.title: Convert '-' to '=' by moving a vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Place a vertical stick onto a minus sign and rotate it to horizontal; the minus gains a second horizontal, becoming an equals sign, while the source of the vertical must remain a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a minus sign and converting it to '=' would resolve the numeric imbalance.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical to '-' to make '=', but the source numeral loses its vertical and becomes invalid.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '=' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Rotate the vertical stick of a plus sign to become a horizontal and place it on the same sign; the plus becomes an equals sign, and the source of the vertical must stay valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus sign and converting it to '=' would fix the numeric imbalance.
matchstick.example: Rotating the vertical of '+' to horizontal to make '=', but the source numeral becomes invalid.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, ignoring the structural constraints of Roman‑numeral glyphs.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before removing a stick, verify that the source numeral will still form a valid Roman numeral after the removal.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the stick move without checking that the resulting expression still contains a left‑hand side, an '=', and a right‑hand side.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After the move, ensure the equation still has exactly one '=', with a valid numeral on each side of the operator(s).

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often stops after producing a syntactically correct equation, forgetting to recompute the values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate the decimal values of both sides after the stick move and confirm they are equal before finalising the answer.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes treats a multi‑step modification as a single action, effectively moving several sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly count the sticks being relocated; only one stick may be removed from its original location and placed elsewhere.

matchstick.description: Creating a non‑canonical Roman numeral (e.g., duplicate V, duplicate L, duplicate D, or more than three I's in a row)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks without checking the formal rules of Roman‑numeral syntax, producing forms like ‘VVIII’ that are not allowed.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move, verify that each numeral conforms to standard Roman‑numeral conventions (no repeated V/L/D, at most three consecutive I's, proper subtractive notation, etc.).
